title: Rotate Right by k
hints: Rotating by `k` is the same as rotating by `k % count` — and guard against an empty array (`% 0` traps).
The result is the last `shift` elements followed by the rest; one-sided range slices make that easy.
`let s = k % nums.count; return Array(nums[(nums.count - s)...] + nums[..<(nums.count - s)])`.
jsBridge: JS: `[...a.slice(-k), ...a.slice(0, -k)]`. Swift uses `ArraySlice` ranges: `a[(n-k)...] + a[..<(n-k)]`. Slices share storage with the original array and keep its indices, a classic gotcha.

compass.q: `let s = a[2...]`: what is `s.startIndex`? Why does `s[0]` crash?
JS `slice` always copies. Swift's `ArraySlice` doesn't. What are the memory implications of storing a tiny slice of a huge array?
The three-reversal trick (O(1) extra space) vs slicing (O(n) extra): when would you pick each?
Carousels and circular buffers rotate indices. Would you rotate data or just map indices with `%`?
